bull.probability_evidence: The bull case's incremental driver beyond the cheap multiples -- LNG-export/data-center demand lifting Appalachian realisations -- is the only claim in either case tagged [Guessing] rather than [Likely]/[Certain] in the evaluation's Bull case paragraph, the weakest-evidenced leg of the thesis, consistent with assigning it the lowest (20%) weight despite the EV/EBITDA re-rating arithmetic itself being straightforward.

target_band.cite: Bull target (73.5) is anchored on EV/EBITDA re-rating from 5.5x to the 5y median 7.4x on TTM EBITDA with net debt at 0.79x EBITDA (factsheet Valuation/Quality, Src RA, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/eqt/financials/ratios/). Deriving per-share TTM figures from the current multiples (price 52.47 / P/E 12.1x = EPS 4.336; price/P/FCF 8.7x = FCF/share 6.031; EBITDA/share 11.140 solved from EV/EBITDA 5.5x and net debt/EBITDA 0.79x) and repricing the SAME TTM fundamentals on the OTHER two multiples at their own 5y medians (factsheet Valuation table: P/E 5y median 12.8x -> implied 55.5; P/FCF 5y median 13.6x -> implied 82.0; EV/EBITDA 5y median 7.4x -> implied 73.6, the target basis) gives a spread of 26.5 between the three anchor-implied prices; half that spread (13.3) / target (73.5) = 0.180.

base.probability_evidence: Management's own raised FY2026 volume guidance and lowered capex (Reuters, 'EQT sees higher 2026 US natgas output on lower spending', 2026-09-22) roughly offsets the 5.93% YoY share dilution discussed in the note's capital-allocation section (research/EQT/2026-10-07.md section 5), with no near-term catalyst identified in either the fact sheet or note to drive a larger re-rating or de-rating within 12 months -- consistent with the base case taking the modal (50%) weight.

target_band.cite: Base target (55.5) is anchored on P/E re-rating from 12.1x to the 5y median 12.8x on flat TTM earnings (factsheet Valuation, Src RA). Using the same TTM-derived per-share fundamentals as the bull calculation (EPS 4.336, FCF/share 6.031, EBITDA/share 11.140, net debt/EBITDA 0.79x; factsheet Valuation/Quality RA), repricing on the OTHER two multiples at their 5y medians gives EV/EBITDA-median implied 73.6 and P/FCF-median implied 82.0, versus the P/E-median implied 55.5 (the target basis); spread 26.5, half-spread 13.3 / target 55.5 = 0.239.

bear.probability_evidence: The bear case rests on facts already realized rather than a forecast: the Q2 2026 EPS miss on weaker gas prices (Reuters, 'EQT misses quarterly profit estimates on weaker natural gas prices', 2026-07-21) and the FY2024 margin collapse to 6.8% operating margin / 1.2% ROIC from FY2023's 49.4% / 11.5% (factsheet Quality table, Src IS/RA) are concrete historical precedent for margin reversion, giving the bear case firmer grounding than the bull case's forward-looking LNG/data-center story -- consistent with a 30% weight, above a symmetric 1/3 default.

target_band.cite: Bear target (45.0) reverts TTM FCF margin (40.4%) to the FY2025 level (34.7%, factsheet Quality, Src CF,IS) at the unchanged current P/FCF 8.7x. Applying the same proportional margin-reversion factor (34.7/40.4=0.859) to EPS and EBITDA/share (derived as for the bull/base calculations) and holding net-debt dollars fixed, then repricing on the OTHER two multiples UNCHANGED (current P/E 12.1x -> implied 45.1; current EV/EBITDA 5.5x -> implied 43.8; factsheet Valuation RA) versus the P/FCF-based target basis of 45.1 gives a spread of only 1.24; half-spread (0.62) / target 45.0 = 0.014 -- a small band because the bear case assumes no multiple re-rating, so the three anchors barely disagree.

jumps.name: Quarterly earnings beat/miss shock (gas-price driven)
jumps.reason: EQT's earnings are highly sensitive to near-term gas prices; Q2 2026 missed Wall Street profit estimates (EPS $0.39 vs $0.42 consensus) on weaker natural gas prices even as volume guidance was raised, and net margin has swung from -16.7% (FY21) to 34.2% (FY23) to 4.6% (FY24) on gas-price cyclicality.
